subject: Data retention: default storage for requests vs generated content
messages:
From: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Questions on default retention for requests vs generated outputs

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this — we're working through vendor selection and need a couple of quick clarifications about Redwood's default retention behavior before we proceed to the procurement checklist. Two fairly specific asks:  

1) When a customer uses the hosted API (no dedicated/private deployment), what is the default retention window for: (a) raw requests (the user prompt / request payload), (b) model-generated outputs (the response text), and (c) any intermediate artifacts (such as logs/trace + KV cache metadata)?

2) Are prompt/request items and model outputs treated differently for deletion or purge requests (e.g., if we ask for data erasure, do outputs persist longer for troubleshooting)?

3) For EU customers, is there an option to ensure both storage and deletion operations remain inside EU regions by default (we want to avoid cross-border replication unless explicitly enabled)?

4) What’s the typical SLA and audit trail for a customer-initiated deletion request (how long until artifacts are purged and how is that reflected in logs)?

We have attached our short vendor security questionnaire (see attachment). If you can provide succinct answers and any links to a public one‑pager, that would be ideal — we may escalate to our procurement and legal teams after that.

Appreciate it,
— Alice Morris
BrightBank Security
Attachment: brightbank_security_questionnaire.pdf

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Morris <alice.morris@brightbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 13:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention for requests vs generated outputs

Alice — thanks, good questions. Below is a concise summary you can share with procurement/legal; I’ve also attached our one‑pager and a short Drive folder with the retention diagrams. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you want to walk through examples.

Executive summary (hosted API defaults):
- Raw requests (prompts / request payloads): retained by default for 30 days. These are used for routing, billing, and incident debugging.
- Model-generated outputs (responses): retained by default for 90 days. We retain outputs longer than raw requests to allow for production troubleshooting (replay + quality investigations) and regression detection.
- Telemetry & intermediate logs (traces, error stacks, KV cache metadata): retained for 180 days by default and rolled into aggregated telemetry used for platform health.

Key clarifications:
- Deletion requests: Customers can raise a data erasure request via the Console or support portal. For hosted API customers, we purge raw requests within 30 days by default; on approved erasure, we prioritize immediate removal of raw prompts and any linked request IDs. Model outputs are scheduled for deletion within 7 days of approval of an erasure request (we keep a short window to ensure no operational regressions).
- Differentiated treatment: Yes — requests and outputs are handled via separate pipelines. Requests are considered primary input and are eligible for expedited removal; outputs are considered derived artifacts and have an additional short retention window for diagnostics unless the customer requests immediate deletion and provides the request identifiers.
- EU residency: Hosted API customers may opt into an EU-only storage configuration during onboarding. For regulated customers, we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) which guarantees EU-only storage and deletion operations (no cross-border replication).
- Audit trail & SLA: Deletion requests generate an immutable audit event and a ticket. For hosted customers, standard target for confirmed purge completion is 7 days; we provide a deletion completion report and a log of purged object IDs. Dedicated/private customers can request faster SLAs via contract.

Next steps I recommend: 1) If you want the EU residency guarantee, request a pinned EU config (we'll route to onboarding), 2) Share any specific regulatory wording you need in an MSA and we can incorporate it into the SOC/Attestation pack, 3) If you need immediate purge of outputs (not the default 7-day), flag that on the deletion request and include example request IDs.

I attached the one‑pager and a short draft answer for procurement to use.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Trust — Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_retention_onepager.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 15:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention for requests vs generated outputs

Grace — quick suggested wording tweaks before we send final to BrightBank (small legal/ops asks):

- Change the "90 days" phrasing to explicitly call out "90 days for hosted-output retention unless customer requests a shorter window" — avoids implication it's immutable.
- Add a one-line on how ephemeral streaming responses are treated (we should note that streaming segments are not separately stored beyond the request/response objects unless tracing is enabled).
- Recommend attaching the Draft Deletion Workflow doc (retention_response_draft.docx) so procurement has a step-by-step.

If you want, I can incorporate into the Drive draft and push a cleaner PDF.

-Karthik

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Morris <alice.morris@brightbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 16:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention for requests vs generated outputs

Alice — following up with an updated, procurement-friendly response and attachments (see Drive link below). I incorporated Karthik's wording suggestions and added a short paragraph on streaming and ephemeral data. Key points again:  

- Defaults: requests 30 days (expedited purge available), outputs 90 days by default but configurable to a shorter policy on request, telemetry 180 days.
- Streaming segments: not stored as discrete artifacts beyond the full request/response object unless tracing is explicitly enabled by the customer; ephemeral streaming fragments are not retained separately.
- EU residency: available as an onboarding option for hosted customers; Redwood Private required for contractual EU-only guarantees.
- Deletion SLA: we aim to complete hosted-account purges within 7 days of confirmed request, with an audit report. Dedicated/private customers can contract faster windows.

Next steps: 
1) If BrightBank wants EU-only defaults we can create a pinned onboarding ticket (I’ve opened HubSpot ticket BRIGHT-1147).
2) I attached a step-by-step deletion workflow and an MSA-friendly paragraph describing the deletion certification we provide.

Suggested calendar: 30-minute call tomorrow at 10am BST to review details and sample deletion report. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to working through this.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Trust — Redwood Inference
